title: RP-HPLC method for simultaneous quantification of free and total thiol groups in native and heat aggregated whey proteins
author: Kurz, Hengst, et al.

steps.title: Prepare 40 mM DTDP stock solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 0.40 mmol 4,4′‑dithiodipyridine (DTDP) in 80 µL of 37 % HCl, then add deionized water to a final volume of 10 mL (40 mM). Store the solution in the dark at 4 °C.

steps.title: Prepare 20 mM EDTA stock (No. 1)
steps.instruction: Dissolve 0.40 mmol EDTA in 10 mL deionized water, adjust the pH to 7 with 1 M NaOH, and bring the volume to 20 mL with deionized water.

steps.title: Prepare 100 mM KH₂PO₄ stock (No. 2)
steps.instruction: Dissolve 10 mmol KH₂PO₄ in deionized water and make up the solution to 100 mL.

steps.title: Prepare 100 mM Na₂HPO₄ stock (No. 3)
steps.instruction: Dissolve 10 mmol Na₂HPO₄ in deionized water and make up the solution to 100 mL.

steps.title: Make pH 5 phosphate buffer (No. 4)
steps.instruction: Mix the 100 mM KH₂PO₄ solution (No. 2) and the 100 mM Na₂HPO₄ solution (No. 3) in the ratio that yields a final pH of 5.

steps.title: Prepare 6 M GdnHCl / 100 mM phosphate / 0.2 mM EDTA buffer (No. 5)
steps.instruction: Dissolve 600 mmol guanidine‑HCl in 70 mL of the KH₂PO₄ solution (No. 2). Add 1 mL of the EDTA stock (No. 1). Add Na₂HPO₄ solution (No. 3) dropwise until the pH reaches 5.0. Finally, bring the volume to 100 mL with the pH 5 phosphate buffer (No. 4).

steps.title: Prepare sample for free‑thiol analysis
steps.instruction: In a reaction tube add 1500 µL of buffer No. 5, then 500 µL of the protein sample, and mix. Add the calculated volume of DTDP stock (No. 0) and shake. Incubate 10 min in the dark (short‑time light exposure does not affect the result). Verify that the pH is 5; if not, adjust with buffer No. 2 or No. 3 (note that any pH adjustment dilutes the sample and must be accounted for). Transfer an aliquot to an amber HPLC vial and proceed to RP‑HPLC detection of 4‑thiopyridine (4‑TP) at 324 nm.

steps.title: Prepare 750 mM KH₂PO₄ stock (No. 6)
steps.instruction: Dissolve 75.0 mmol KH₂PO₄ in deionized water and make up to 100 mL.

steps.title: Prepare 750 mM Na₂HPO₄ stock (No. 7)
steps.instruction: Dissolve 75.2 mmol Na₂HPO₄ in deionized water and make up to 100 mL.

steps.title: Make pH 5 phosphate buffer (No. 8)
steps.instruction: Mix the 750 mM KH₂PO₄ solution (No. 6) and the 750 mM Na₂HPO₄ solution (No. 7) in the ratio that yields a final pH of 5.

steps.title: Prepare 6 M GdnHCl / 750 mM phosphate / 0.31 mM EDTA buffer (No. 9)
steps.instruction: Dissolve 600 mmol guanidine‑HCl in 70 mL of the KH₂PO₄ stock (No. 6). Add 1.55 mL of the EDTA stock (No. 1). Add Na₂HPO₄ solution (No. 7) dropwise until pH 5.0, then bring the volume to 100 mL with buffer No. 8.

steps.title: Prepare 6 M GdnHCl / 0.5 M Tris solution (No. 10)
steps.instruction: Dissolve 50 mmol Tris(hydroxymethyl)aminomethane and 600 mmol guanidine‑HCl in deionized water and make up to 100 mL.

steps.title: Prepare 30 % (w/v) NaBH₄ in 1 M NaOH (No. 11)
steps.instruction: Dissolve 40 mmol sodium borohydride in 5 mL of 1 M NaOH; this solution is used fresh.

steps.title: Reduce disulfide bonds and prepare sample for total‑thiol analysis
steps.instruction: Add 1000 µL of protein sample to 770 µL of solution No. 10 and mix. Add 230 µL freshly prepared NaBH₄ solution (No. 11) and mix. Carefully overlay 50 µL 1‑octanol to prevent foaming. Incubate the mixture at 65 °C for 60 min. Quench the reaction by adding 400 µL of 5 M HCl (pierce the octanol layer with the pipette and mix). Wait 10 min for completion. Add the calculated volume of DTDP stock (No. 0) and mix; wait another 10 min. Filter the reaction mixture through a 0.45 µm RC‑extra syringe filter. Transfer 500 µL of the filtrate to an amber HPLC vial and add 1000 µL of buffer No. 9; close the vial and mix well. Determine total thiol concentration by RP‑HPLC.

steps.title: Prepare L‑cysteine calibration standards
steps.instruction: Make a 10 mM L‑cysteine hydrochloride monohydrate stock by dissolving 1 mmol in deionized water and bringing the volume to 100 mL (No. 12). Dilute this stock to 5.0, 2.5, 1.0 and 0.5 mM with deionized water. For each concentration transfer 1850 µL of buffer No. 5 into a reaction tube, add 100 µL of the appropriate cysteine solution and 50 µL DTDP stock (No. 0). Incubate 10 min, then transfer 1000 µL of each mixture into amber HPLC vials.

steps.title: Run RP‑HPLC analysis
steps.instruction:
Use an Agilent 1100 series system equipped with a Zorbax 300SB‑C18‑3.5 µm (4.6 × 150 mm) column and a Zorbax 300SB‑C18‑5 µm (4.6 × 12.5 mm) pre‑column. Set injection volume to 20 µL, column oven to 40 °C, and flow rate to 1 mL min⁻¹. Apply the gradient of Table 1 (Solvent A: water + 0.2 % v/v TFA; Solvent B: acetonitrile + 0.2 % v/v TFA) as follows:
Time (min) – %A – %B
0.0 – 98 – 2
1.5 – 98 – 2
1.5 – 98 – 2
5.0 – 98 – 2
6.0 – 94 – 6
6.5 – 0 – 100
7.0 – 0 – 100
8.0 – 98 – 2
10.0 – 98 – 2
Detect at 324 nm with a diode‑array detector, integrate peaks with Agilent ChemStation (Rev. B.04.03), and record the total run time of 10 min.

steps.title: Quantify thiols in samples
steps.instruction: Measure the peak area of 4‑thiopyridine (4‑TP) at 324 nm for each sample and each calibration standard. Generate a calibration curve from the cysteine standards (peak area vs. 4‑TP concentration). Use the curve to calculate the concentration of free or total thiols in the unknown samples.
